testcase.name: liveness truthfully distinguishes an unconfigured platform from a ready one
installation status is public-safe and contains no bootstrap material
readiness is a safe 503 while dependencies and authentication are unconfigured
normal entry point keeps all MFA and recovery operations disabled
public owner-setup and login declarations cannot report operational success
all protected resource and session routes deny anonymous and forged authority
request validation blocks caller authority fields and keeps Add Domain one-field
body size, content type and malformed JSON have safe consistent errors
anonymous callers cannot probe resource validation or bypass authorization using retry headers
deployment and routing declarations remain unavailable and reject command injection
unknown routes return JSON errors and request IDs are server-owned
OpenAPI is valid, matches generated artifacts and labels unavailable endpoints
the local API documentation is readable with request submission disabled
missing route policy denies access even with a valid server principal
public routes work without a session store and never create owner authority
forged headers, body fields and request.user cannot authenticate
expired, boundary-expired, revoked and malformed sessions are denied
agent/API-key identities and future non-owner roles cannot become a human owner
owner context comes only from the resolver, is frozen and cannot bleed across requests
session store failures deny access with a sanitized availability error
database configuration has no ambient defaults, remote hosts or URL overrides
host PG environment settings cannot replace the configured identity, port or TLS policy
an unconfigured database does not connect using PG environment fallbacks
an unreachable database returns only a coarse unavailable state
migration history rejects altered, unknown, duplicate and non-prefix releases
failed rollback discards the client exactly once and redacts driver errors
connection and commit-acknowledgement failures are redacted without promising rollback
migration CLI rejects arbitrary paths/arguments and never prints configured secrets
RFC 6238 SHA1 vectors match six-digit TOTP and reject replay
AES-GCM uses independent nonces and binds the installation and user; wrong keys and corruption fail
review preparation rejects missing or malformed MFA keys before any password work
opaque credentials are canonical, purpose-separated and never authority-bearing IDs
duplicate, encoded and oversized cookie credentials are rejected
real Argon2id hashing preserves long/unicode passwords, salts independently and fails closed on unsupported PHC costs
password hashing admits two operations and rejects excess work without queuing
owner contract enforces length/UTF-8 limits and rejects caller authority
review origin configuration rejects HTTP, credentials, paths and noncanonical origins
factory rejects review activation without TLS and in production; main has no activation path
project cursor is a strict canonical position marker, never a workspace override
project store fails closed and redacts an unavailable connection before any query can run
resource IDs reject demo identifiers, nil values and non-v4 UUIDs
create-project accepts bounded data but never caller workspace/owner authority
Add Domain is exactly one field, with no mode or verification shortcut
pagination limits and opaque cursor syntax are bounded
static deployment requests cannot inject a host command or container options
agent structure accepts a typed candidate, without claiming signature/expiry/ownership verification
agent contract rejects generic operations, unsafe mounts, injected fields and inverted timestamps
auth client restricts secret submission to its canonical HTTPS origin
auth client sends cookies, custom header and memory-only rotating CSRF; redirect following is disabled
password responses cannot masquerade as full sessions; unverified session responses are denied
auth client sanitizes API errors and rejects HTML or redirects without echoing secrets
boundaries allow a portable contract and separate consumers
boundaries reject a browser import of API implementation or agent contract
boundaries reject Node-only contract imports and direct API host execution
required gate rejects failed, cancelled, skipped and missing jobs
progress event selection uses validated base SHAs for PRs, merge queues and pushes
discovery and missing browser markers cannot count as browser execution
workflow validation accepts the actual policy and rejects weakened gates
installer checks cannot be omitted, skipped or moved off the pinned target
CI command capture preserves nonzero status and records a failed step
browser job reruns retain the verified artifact identity
fixture upload rejects download-only inputs and missing names or output IDs
loopback harness separates static/demo, typed HTTP fixtures and the real unconfigured API
HTTP requests validate a real session before fetching protected data and include cookies
a rejected session does not request protected data or fall back to fixtures
HTML and malformed JSON are reported as invalid API responses
a forged or malformed success session cannot unlock the overview request
HTTP overview data rejects synthetic IDs, unbounded metrics and unknown fields
malformed server error envelopes never surface arbitrary response text
streamed responses are bounded even without a Content-Length header
request cancellation propagates instead of becoming a network error
bounded overview accepts the full metadata contract including escaped descriptions, then cancels above 4 MiB
database tests refuse absent opt-in, non-loopback hosts and non-disposable database names
CI rejects a missing, unpinned, optional or disconnected PostgreSQL test gate
project client rejects insecure/cross-origin targets and unverified sessions before mutation
project client binds create to current MFA CSRF and retains the caller retry key across ambiguous failures
project list/detail/create responses reject foreign workspace scope and mismatched environment links
project errors never echo raw response text and definitive conflicts are not ambiguous
